transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-14
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Patel (Redwood AE); Daniel Kim (Redwood SE); Priya Raman (NexaHealth - Head of Security); Ethan Cole (NexaHealth - Cloud Architect); Marta Silva (NexaHealth - Compliance)

Summary:
Short: Security review focused on encryption at rest and in transit, KMS integrations (CMEK/BYOK), HSM-backed keys, audit logs and compliance requirements for NexaHealth's PHI workloads. Customer wants details on key custody, rotation, audit trail, and impact on latency/availability for Private deployment.
Topics: encryption at rest (envelope encryption, AES-256-GCM), in-transit (TLS), BYOK onboarding, HSM vs cloud KMS, audit logging export, key rotation/rotation windows, legal/data residency considerations.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Sophie (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro \u0014 I'm Sophie, AE at Redwood, and with me is Daniel, our solutions engineer.
[00:00:10] Priya (NexaHealth): Hi, thanks. Priya here. We run the security program, focusing on PHI handling and the compliance stack.
[00:00:15] Ethan (NexaHealth): Ethan, cloud infra. We'll mostly focus on key management and latency impact.
[00:00:20] Marta (NexaHealth): Marta from compliance, I'll jump in on audit and evidence needs.
[00:00:25] Daniel (Redwood SE): Great, thanks. Agenda \u0014 encryption at rest/in transit, KMS options (CMEK/BYOK), HSM requirements, audit logs, and next steps. We'll try to keep it practical.
[00:00:40] Sophie: Quick question \u0014 are you evaluating Hosted API or Private? I think you mentioned Private in the notes.
[00:00:46] Priya: Correct, Private deployment is what we're leaning to because of PHI and our risk model. We need full control over keys, ideally HSM-backed.
[00:00:56] Daniel: Understood. I'll describe our typical architecture and where KMS fits in. At a high level, Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations and also BYOK with HSM-backed keys where customers hold custody. We use envelope encryption \u0014 so application data is encrypted with data keys (AES-256), and those data keys are wrapped by a customer-managed master key.
[00:01:15] Ethan: When you say wrapped, is that envelope handled in our VPC or in Redwood's control plane? We need to ensure the unwrapped data key never leaves customer control.
[00:01:25] Daniel: Good call. In Private deployment, the KMS calls are made from the customer's VPC \u0014 the key material stays in the customer's KMS/HSM. Redwood only receives encrypted data keys. For hosted, we support customer-managed keys but obviously the control plane is hosted; for Private, we can run the control plane in your environment so keys never surface to Redwood.
[00:01:45] Priya: Can you support HSMs that are FIPS 140-2/140-3 compliant? Our policy requires HSM-backed master keys for production PHI.
[00:01:53] Daniel: Yes, we integrate with major cloud HSM offerings \u0014 AWS CloudHSM, Google Cloud HSM, Azure Dedicated HSM \u0014 and we have a documented BYOK flow for bringing customer key material. We also support KMS-backed keys where the KMS uses an HSM under the hood.
[00:02:07] Marta: Do you have documented evidence for HSM usage and FIPS attestations? We need artifacts for audits.
[00:02:12] Sophie: We'll send SOC 2 and ISO artifacts and a whitepaper about HSM integrations. We have attestation links for the cloud KMS providers; for on-prem HSMs we'll provide integration docs.
[00:02:22] Ethan: Performance question \u0014 what is the latency impact when using remote KMS calls for every token or request? We can't have per-token KMS calls at runtime.
[00:02:32] Daniel: We avoid per-token KMS calls by using envelope encryption and local data key caching in the runtime. The flow: on startup or first access, the service requests a wrapped data key from KMS, unwraps in the runtime (or receives wrapped and decrypts locally with HSM if in VPC), and then caches the data key in memory with TTL. We also support KV cache for prefix results \u0014 but note, any persisted caches are encrypted with the data key.
[00:02:55] Ethan: So cache TTLs and key rotation are important \u0014 if you rotate the master key, how do you re-encrypt data keys and cached artifacts?
[00:03:05] Daniel: We support key rotation policies. For rotation, we re-wrap existing data keys with the new master key; cached tokens in memory continue until TTL expiry. For long-term storage (snapshots/backups), we recommend a re-encryption job that uses the active master key. We'll provide a migration script.
[00:03:18] Priya: Is there any scenario where Redwood has access to plaintext keys? We need explicit guarantee that Redwood personnel cannot decrypt customer data.
[00:03:26] Sophie: For Private deployments where the control plane and KMS are customer-managed, Redwood personnel do not have access to plaintext. For hosted, we offer BYOK with limited key access models but since the KMS is customer-managed, we still don't get plaintext. We'll clarify the threat model in the follow-up doc.
[00:03:42] Marta: Auditability \u0014 we need KMS logs, key usage logs, and a consolidated audit trail for both KMS calls and Redwood API calls that access PHI. Can you export logs to our SIEM?
[00:03:52] Daniel: Yes \u0014 we support exporting audit logs to syslog/S3 or Pub/Sub. In Private deployments, logs can be shipped directly to your logging stack. We also instrument token-level tracing so you can correlate KMS usage with API requests.
[00:04:06] Priya: For compliance we also need proof of tamper-evident logs and retention policies.
[00:04:11] Daniel: We integrate with immutable storage for audit logs and can support retention/time-based hold policies as part of the deployment config.
[00:04:20] Ethan: Key format question \u0014 do you require a specific key algorithm? We currently standardize on RSA-3072 for signing and AES-256-GCM for data keys.
[00:04:29] Daniel: That's fine \u0014 for data encryption we use AES-256-GCM. For key wrapping we rely on your KMS's wrapping algorithm; most cloud KMS do AES-KW or RSA-OAEP depending on key type. We'll document supported algorithms per provider.
[00:04:40] Priya: BYOK process \u0014 what are the steps and how long does it typically take to onboard a key?
[00:04:46] Daniel: Typically: 1) agree on HSM vendor and key policy, 2) create key in your KMS/HSM or import key material using the vendor's key import tool, 3) share key identifiers and policies with Redwood, 4) perform a test rotation and decrypt/encrypt flow in staging. For cloud KMS it's often 2-3 days; for on-prem HSM import there may be scheduling and more time \u0014 1-2 weeks depending on approvals.
[00:05:05] Marta: How do you handle backups and snapshots \u0014 are they encrypted at rest with the same data keys? If we remove a key, is there a process for destroying backups?
[00:05:12] Daniel: Backups are encrypted with the same envelope approach. If you retire a master key, we require a re-encrypt or key escrow plan. For private deployments, deletion policies are customer-controlled. We'll provide runbooks for key retirement and backup re-encryption.
[00:05:26] Sophie: Quick interjection \u0014 a few of our customers want an HSM escrow model where they maintain a secondary key copy to recover in emergencies. We can support documented escrow procedures but those are subject to your governance.
[00:05:36] Priya: Regarding HSM vendors: we use Thales and AWS CloudHSM in different environments. Do you have a preference or special integration?
[00:05:43] Daniel: We have tested integrations with CloudHSM and Thales Luna. For Thales, we'll need the PKCS#11 interface details; for CloudHSM we use the standard KMS endpoints. We'll share the integration checklist.
[00:05:53] Ethan: Networking \u0014 for Private, does Redwood need open egress to the internet for KMS or can it be fully private inside our VPC/peering?
[00:06:00] Daniel: Private can be fully inside your VPC with VPC endpoints to cloud KMS or direct HSM connectivity. We can support no-public-internet deployments. For hosted flows, some egress is necessary unless you use a dedicated peering arrangement.
[00:06:11] Priya: TLS and in-transit encryption \u0014 standard? We require TLS 1.2+ and mutal TLS for some admin endpoints.
[00:06:16] Daniel: We support TLS 1.2 and 1.3; mutual TLS can be configured for control plane admin interfaces in Private. We'll include the cipher suites we support.
[00:06:26] Marta: Evidence for forensic purposes: do you offer request-level logs with user identity and request payload hashes? We can't have full payload in logs.
[00:06:33] Daniel: Correct \u0014 logs are hashed/redacted. We record request metadata, identity (SSO subject), timestamp, and a SHA-256 of the payload to enable audit without storing plaintext.
[00:06:44] Sophie: On SSO and RBAC \u0014 Redwood integrates with SAML/SCIM for provisioning and RBAC. You can map roles to key access policies so only specific service identities can request unwrap operations.
[00:06:55] Priya: Can we restrict which Redwood service accounts can use which keys? We need separation of duties.
[00:07:00] Daniel: Yes, we support principal-bound policies and least-privilege role mapping. In Private you fully control IAM and can use resource policies to limit access.
[00:07:09] Marta: Any third-party audits for the Redwood codepath that touches keys?
[00:07:13] Sophie: We have SOC 2 and ISO certifications for the platform. We'll send the report and a redacted architecture diagram showing where keys are used.
[00:07:20] Ethan: Edge case: if KMS provider goes down, what is failover? Do you support multi-region KMS or key replication?
[00:07:28] Daniel: You can configure multi-region key replicas where supported; we also recommend a multi-KMS fallback where a secondary key can be used. There are caveats for consistency during rotation. We'll outline recommended patterns.
[00:07:40] Priya: One more \u0014 legal/data residency. Our PHI must remain in the EU region. Can keys and data be constrained to EU-only?
[00:07:46] Daniel: Yes, with Private deployment you can pin region and ensure KMS and HSM are in EU regions. For hosted, we'd need to confirm region support for your account; we have EU regions available.
[00:07:58] Marta: For the audit we'll want the list of controls mapped to SOC 2 and ISO clauses.
[00:08:03] Sophie: We'll add a controls mapping doc to the packet.
[00:08:08] (silence / side chatter)
[00:58:12] [note: omitted middle discussion for brevity in this export]
[01:00:10] Daniel: To summarize the technical takeaway: envelope encryption, support for HSM-backed CMEK/BYOK, local data key caching to avoid per-request KMS latency, log export to your SIEM, and runbooks for rotation/retirement.
[01:00:28] Priya: That all sounds good. I want the whitepapers and the HSM onboarding checklist. We'll also need a timeline and cost for Private deployment with HSM nodes.
[01:00:35] Sophie: We'll get those over \u0014 Daniel will share the HSM whitepaper and example config, I'll send the SOC 2/ISO artifacts and a pricing ballpark.
[01:00:42] Ethan: After we get the docs we'll schedule the infra deep-dive. 30-45 minutes to run benchmarks and test integration.
[01:00:50] Marta: We'll also need evidence for our compliance review \u0014 log snapshots and key usage examples.
[01:00:55] Sophie: Noted. Anything else?
[01:01:00] Priya: No, that's it. Thanks.
[01:01:03] Sophie: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the packet by Monday.
